IMPLEMENT THIS EXACT APPROVED LESSON CONTENT:

SUBJECT:
Science

GRADE:
Grade 1

LESSON:
Lesson 2

TITLE:
Plants & Animals 🌿🐾

SUBTITLE:
Discover how plants and animals are alike, how they are different, and what they need to live.

ESTIMATED TIME:
20–25 minutes

==================================================
LEARNING GOALS 🎯
==================================================

By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to:

• Identify plants and animals as living things.
• Describe basic needs shared by plants and animals.
• Recognize important parts of common plants and animals.
• Explain simple differences between plants and animals.
• Match plants and animals to places where they can live.

==================================================
OPENING — TWO KINDS OF LIVING THINGS 🌱🐕
==================================================

In Lesson 1, we learned that living things grow, need resources, respond to their surroundings, and have life cycles.

Now let's look more closely at two important groups of living things:

🌿 Plants

and

🐾 Animals

Plants and animals can look very different.

A sunflower does not look like a puppy.

A fish does not look like a tree.

But plants and animals are both living things.

They both need resources from their environment.

They both grow and change.

They both have parts that help them live.

==================================================
SECTION 1 — WHAT IS A PLANT? 🌱
==================================================

A plant is a living thing.

Plants come in many shapes and sizes.

Some are tiny.

Some grow into very tall trees. 🌳

Examples of plants include:

🌻 Sunflowers
🌳 Trees
🌵 Cacti
🌾 Grass
🌿 Ferns
🌹 Roses

Most plants stay rooted in one place.

But staying in one place does NOT mean they are nonliving.

Plants grow, use resources, respond to their surroundings, and have life cycles.

==================================================
VISUAL 1 — MANY KINDS OF PLANTS
==================================================

Create a child-friendly visual containing:

🌻 flowering plant
🌳 tree
🌵 cactus
🌾 grass
🌿 fern

Label:

"Plants can look different, but they are all living things."

==================================================
SECTION 2 — BASIC PARTS OF A PLANT 🌱
==================================================

Plants have parts that help them survive.

Let's learn four important parts.

--------------------------------------------------
ROOTS
--------------------------------------------------

Roots are usually found under the ground.

Roots help:

• hold the plant in place;
• take in water;
• take in minerals from the soil.

Think of roots as the plant's underground support system.

--------------------------------------------------
STEM
--------------------------------------------------

The stem helps hold the plant upright.

It also helps move water and other materials through the plant.

Some stems are soft and green.

Tree trunks are also stems.

--------------------------------------------------
LEAVES 🍃
--------------------------------------------------

Leaves help the plant make food using light energy.

Many leaves are green.

Leaves also exchange gases with the air.

--------------------------------------------------
FLOWERS 🌸
--------------------------------------------------

Many plants produce flowers.

Flowers can help plants make seeds.

Not every plant has obvious flowers, but many familiar plants do.

==================================================
VISUAL 2 — PARTS OF A PLANT
==================================================

Create a clear labeled diagram of a simple flowering plant.

Labels:

🌸 Flower
🍃 Leaf
🌱 Stem
🌿 Roots

Use large labels and arrows.

Caption:

"Different plant parts have different jobs."

==================================================
SECTION 3 — WHAT DO PLANTS NEED? ☀️💧
==================================================

Plants need resources to live and grow.

Many plants need:

☀️ light

💧 water

🌬️ air

🌱 nutrients

🏡 enough space and a suitable place to grow

Plants use light energy to help make sugars they can use for energy and growth.

Roots take in water and minerals.

Leaves help the plant capture light.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE 🌻
--------------------------------------------------

Imagine a sunflower growing outside.

It receives light from the Sun.

Its roots take in water.

Its leaves capture light.

Its stem supports the plant.

Together, these parts help the sunflower live and grow.

==================================================
SECTION 4 — WHAT IS AN ANIMAL? 🐾
==================================================

An animal is also a living thing.

Animals come in many shapes and sizes.

Examples include:

🐕 Dog
🐈 Cat
🐦 Bird
🐟 Fish
🦋 Butterfly
🐘 Elephant
🐸 Frog

Animals usually move from place to place during at least part of their lives.

Animals get energy by eating food.

Different animals eat different things.

Some eat plants.

Some eat other animals.

Some eat both.

==================================================
VISUAL 3 — MANY KINDS OF ANIMALS
==================================================

Create a child-friendly visual containing:

🐕 dog
🐦 bird
🐟 fish
🦋 butterfly
🐸 frog

Caption:

"Animals can look very different, but they are all living things."

==================================================
SECTION 5 — ANIMAL BODY PARTS 🐕
==================================================

Animals have body parts that help them survive.

Different animals have different parts.

--------------------------------------------------
LEGS 🐾
--------------------------------------------------

Many animals use legs to:

• walk;
• run;
• jump;
• climb.

Dogs, cats, frogs, and many other animals have legs.

--------------------------------------------------
WINGS 🪽
--------------------------------------------------

Many birds and insects have wings.

Wings can help some animals fly.

--------------------------------------------------
FINS 🐟
--------------------------------------------------

Fish use fins to help them move and steer through water.

--------------------------------------------------
EYES 👀
--------------------------------------------------

Eyes help many animals see their surroundings.

--------------------------------------------------
EARS 👂
--------------------------------------------------

Ears help many animals detect sounds.

Not every animal has ears that look like ours.

--------------------------------------------------
MOUTHS OR BEAKS
--------------------------------------------------

Animals use mouths or beaks to take in food.

A bird may use its beak.

A dog uses its mouth.

==================================================
SECTION 6 — DIFFERENT PARTS FOR DIFFERENT ANIMALS 🐟🦅🐸
==================================================

Animal bodies are not all the same.

Different body parts can help animals live in different places.

A fish has fins that help it swim. 🐟

A bird has wings that may help it fly. 🐦

A frog has strong back legs that help it jump. 🐸

A duck has webbed feet that help it move through water. 🦆

💡 IMPORTANT:

Animals do not need to have the same body parts to be animals.

Different animals have different structures that help them survive.

==================================================
VISUAL 4 — ANIMAL PARTS AND THEIR JOBS
==================================================

Create a simple comparison:

🐟 Fish
Fins → swimming

🐦 Bird
Wings → flying or moving through the air

🐸 Frog
Strong legs → jumping

🐕 Dog
Legs → walking and running

Caption:

"Animal body parts help animals move and survive."

==================================================
SECTION 7 — WHAT DO ANIMALS NEED? 💧🍎
==================================================

Animals need resources too.

Most animals need:

💧 water

🌬️ air

🍎 food

🏡 shelter or a safe place

🌿 enough space to live

Different animals need different kinds of food and habitats.

A rabbit may eat plants. 🐇

A lion eats other animals. 🦁

A bear may eat both plants and animals. 🐻

For Grade 1, remember:

"Animals get energy by eating food."

==================================================
SECTION 8 — PLANTS AND ANIMALS ARE ALIKE 🤝
==================================================

Plants and animals are different, but they also have things in common.

Both are living things.

Both:

💧 need water;

⚡ need energy;

🌱 grow and change;

🌬️ interact with their environment;

🐣 have life cycles.

This means a tree and a dog may look very different, but both show signs of life.

==================================================
VISUAL 5 — PLANTS AND ANIMALS: WHAT THEY SHARE
==================================================

Create a simple Venn-style comparison.

LEFT:
PLANTS 🌿

• usually stay rooted
• use light to help make food
• have roots, stems, and leaves

RIGHT:
ANIMALS 🐾

• eat food
• usually move from place to place
• have different body parts for movement and sensing

MIDDLE:
BOTH ❤️

• are living
• need water
• need energy
• grow
• respond
• have life cycles

Keep wording short and large enough for a Grade 1 learner.

==================================================
SECTION 9 — HOW ARE PLANTS AND ANIMALS DIFFERENT? 🌿 VS 🐕
==================================================

Plants and animals have some important differences.

--------------------------------------------------
PLANTS
--------------------------------------------------

Most plants stay rooted in one place.

Plants use light energy to help make their own food.

Plants often have:

🌿 roots
🌱 stems
🍃 leaves
🌸 flowers

--------------------------------------------------
ANIMALS
--------------------------------------------------

Animals get energy by eating food.

Many animals can move from place to place.

Animals can have:

🐾 legs
🪽 wings
🐟 fins
👀 eyes
👂 ears
🦷 teeth or beaks

Different animals may have different body parts.

==================================================
SECTION 10 — WHERE DO PLANTS AND ANIMALS LIVE? 🏡
==================================================

A habitat is a place where a living thing lives and gets what it needs.

Different living things live in different habitats.

--------------------------------------------------
FOREST 🌳
--------------------------------------------------

Forests may contain:

🌳 trees
🐦 birds
🦌 deer
🐿️ squirrels

--------------------------------------------------
POND OR LAKE 💧
--------------------------------------------------

Freshwater habitats may contain:

🐟 fish
🐸 frogs
🌿 water plants

--------------------------------------------------
GRASSLAND 🌾
--------------------------------------------------

Grasslands may contain:

🌾 grasses
🐇 rabbits
🦋 insects
🐦 birds

--------------------------------------------------
GARDEN 🌻
--------------------------------------------------

Gardens may contain:

🌻 flowers
🌿 vegetables
🐝 bees
🦋 butterflies

A habitat provides resources that living things need.

==================================================
VISUAL 6 — MATCH THE HABITAT
==================================================

Create four simple habitat panels:

🌳 Forest
💧 Pond
🌾 Grassland
🌻 Garden

Show 1–2 suitable plants or animals in each.

Caption:

"Living things live where they can find the resources they need."

==================================================
SECTION 11 — STEP-BY-STEP: IS IT A PLANT OR AN ANIMAL? 🧠
==================================================

Suppose we see a sunflower.

How can we classify it?

STEP 1:
Look at its parts.

It has roots, a stem, leaves, and a flower.

STEP 2:
Ask how it gets energy.

It uses light energy to help make food.

STEP 3:
Ask whether it is rooted in place.

Yes.

CONCLUSION:

🌻 A sunflower is a plant.

--------------------------------------------------

Now think about a rabbit.

STEP 1:
Look at its body.

It has legs, eyes, ears, and a mouth.

STEP 2:
Ask how it gets energy.

It eats food.

STEP 3:
Ask how it moves.

It can hop and move from place to place.

CONCLUSION:

🐇 A rabbit is an animal.

==================================================
WORKED EXAMPLE — PLANT OR ANIMAL? 🦋
==================================================

We see a butterfly.

Let's investigate.

STEP 1:
Does it have roots and leaves?

No.

STEP 2:
Does it eat or take in food?

Yes.

STEP 3:
Can it move from place to place?

Yes.

STEP 4:
Does it have animal body parts?

Yes.

It has wings, legs, eyes, and other animal structures.

CONCLUSION:

🦋 A butterfly is an animal.

==================================================
GUIDED EXAMPLE — WHAT DOES THIS PLANT PART DO? 🍃
==================================================

Suppose we look at a leaf.

What is one important job of a leaf?

A leaf helps the plant capture light.

Plants use light energy to help make food.

So:

🍃 Leaf → helps capture light for the plant.

==================================================
SECTION 12 — BABY AND ADULT ANIMALS 🐣➡️🐔
==================================================

Animals grow and change during their lives.

A baby animal may look similar to its adult form.

A puppy grows into an adult dog. 🐶➡️🐕

A kitten grows into an adult cat. 🐱➡️🐈

Some animals change more dramatically.

A caterpillar can become a butterfly. 🐛➡️🦋

A tadpole can grow into a frog. 🐸

These changes are part of an animal's life cycle.

==================================================
SECTION 13 — PLANTS HAVE LIFE CYCLES TOO 🌱
==================================================

Plants also have life cycles.

A simple flowering plant life cycle may look like:

Seed 🌰
↓

Sprout 🌱
↓

Young Plant 🪴
↓

Adult Plant 🌻
↓

Seeds

Then the cycle can begin again.

==================================================
VISUAL 7 — TWO SIMPLE LIFE CYCLES
==================================================

Create two side-by-side sequences.

PLANT:

Seed
→ Sprout
→ Plant
→ New seeds

ANIMAL EXAMPLE:

Egg
→ Chick
→ Adult chicken

or another simple age-appropriate animal example.

Caption:

"Plants and animals grow and change during their life cycles."

==================================================
SECTION 14 — HOW PLANTS AND ANIMALS CAN HELP EACH OTHER 🌻🐝
==================================================

Plants and animals often share the same environment.

Sometimes they can help each other.

For example:

🐝 A bee may visit a flower to collect nectar.

🌸 While visiting flowers, bees can help move pollen from flower to flower.

🐦 Some animals eat fruits and can carry seeds to new places.

🌳 Plants can provide food and shelter for animals.

Living things are connected to their environments and to other living things.

For Grade 1, remember:

"Plants and animals can depend on each other."

==================================================
COMMON MISTAKES ⚠️
==================================================

MISTAKE 1:

"Plants are not living because they do not walk."

❌ Not true.

Plants grow, use resources, respond, and have life cycles.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 2:

"All animals have four legs."

❌ Not true.

Birds, fish, insects, snakes, and many other animals have different body structures.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 3:

"Plants get food by eating like animals."

❌ Not true.

Plants use light energy, water, and gases to help make sugars they can use.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 4:

"Every animal lives on land."

❌ Not true.

Fish and many other animals live in water.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 5:

"Every plant has a flower."

❌ Not true.

Many plants have flowers, but not all plants produce obvious flowers.

==================================================
ACTIVITY — PLANT OR ANIMAL? 🌿🐾
==================================================

Look at each example.

🌻 Sunflower
🐕 Dog
🌳 Tree
🐟 Fish
🌵 Cactus
🦋 Butterfly

Sort them.

PLANTS 🌿

🌻 Sunflower
🌳 Tree
🌵 Cactus

ANIMALS 🐾

🐕 Dog
🐟 Fish
🦋 Butterfly

Now ask:

"What clues helped you decide?"

Good clues include:

• plant parts;
• animal body parts;
• how the organism gets energy;
• how it moves;
• where it lives.

==================================================
ACTIVITY — MATCH THE PART TO ITS JOB 🔎
==================================================

ROOTS 🌿
→ take in water and help hold a plant in place

LEAVES 🍃
→ help capture light

STEM 🌱
→ supports the plant and helps move materials

FINS 🐟
→ help a fish swim

WINGS 🪽
→ help many birds and insects move through the air

LEGS 🐾
→ help many animals walk, run, jump, or climb

==================================================
QUICK CHECK 🧠
==================================================

1. SUNFLOWER 🌻

Plant or animal?

Answer:
Plant

Why?
It has plant structures such as roots, a stem, leaves, and a flower.

--------------------------------------------------

2. FISH 🐟

Plant or animal?

Answer:
Animal

Why?
It eats food and has animal body structures such as fins.

--------------------------------------------------

3. ROOT 🌿

What kind of living thing has roots?

Answer:
Plant

Why?
Roots are important plant structures.

--------------------------------------------------

4. WING 🪽

Which group often has animals with wings?

Answer:
Animals

Why?
Birds and many insects use wings.

--------------------------------------------------

5. DO PLANTS AND ANIMALS BOTH NEED WATER? 💧

Answer:
Yes

Why?
Water is an important resource for both plants and animals.

==================================================
KEY CONCEPT ⭐
==================================================

TITLE:

Plants and animals are different kinds of living things.

BODY:

Plants and animals both need resources, grow, respond to their environments, and have life cycles.

Plants often have roots, stems, and leaves and use light to help make food.

Animals eat food and have body parts that help them move, sense, and survive.

==================================================
FINAL RECAP 🌟
==================================================

Remember:

🌿 Plants are living things.

🐾 Animals are living things.

💧 Both need resources such as water.

🌱 Both grow and change.

🍃 Plants have parts such as roots, stems, and leaves.

🐟 Animals can have parts such as legs, wings, fins, eyes, and ears.

☀️ Plants use light energy to help make food.

🍎 Animals get energy by eating food.

🏡 Plants and animals live in habitats where they can get what they need.

🐣 Both have life cycles.
